notes.title: Tlahuelpuchi
notes.content:
Today we are presenting to you one of many [b]terrifying creatures[/b] you'll have to face in the dangerous world of [i]Mictlan[/i].

[h3]Tlahuelpuchi: a blood-sucking creature.[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38746200/2e6a2523078edd3208b1003c4ccb07f0f97c522a.jpg[/img]

The Tlahuelpuchi are mythological beings of [b]Tlaxcala folklore[/b], whose origin is still debated among specialists.

Usually female, these creatures were [b]born with a curse[/b] that would accompany them forever. 
The witches had the ability to transform themselves into several animals, such as buzzards, cats, dogs and turkeys. The power to [b]shape-shift[/b] usually came around the age of puberty. At this time, the young Tlahuelpuchi began to crave human blood. 

Their [b]bloodthirst[/b] could only be satisfied by feeding on the blood of [b]infants[/b], who they kidnapped from their rural communities, fleeing to the mountains. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38746200/a16c4ef46d4361a9ac098e0f2e34b322323a680b.jpg[/img]

One of the places where the Tlahuelpuchi met to plot their evils, were the ruins of the[b] temple of Teopanzolco[/b], which was located between Atla and Xolotla, over a hill where, at night, you could see a long line of [b]fireballs[/b]: one of the forms that the Tlahuelpuchi used in order to travel over the skies.

These creatures could actually also [b]live incognito[/b] in their villages, that's why, even in modern folklore, couples with children and women with unbaptized babies [b]protect themselves [/b]and their families by putting orange branches on the roof or their clothes upside down near the crib of the infant, or even by positioning cross-shaped objects under it.

As a matter of fact, the belief in these otherwordly beings has[b] remained alive[/b] until well into the twentieth century in some villages in Mexico. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38746200/8f099501207ea502bce481a03e277cef473f4551.jpg[/img] [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38746200/192335d4cf51442ed25917e22539e09a0d1f17b2.jpg[/img]

In [i]Mictlan[/i], the Tlahuelpuchi will be [b]adversaries for you to defeat[/b]. 

For their design, we seek to recreate lunar elements, referring to figures such as the [b]goddess Coyolxauhqu[/b]i and the [b]Tzitzimimes[/b], which are the most common inspirations for contemporary Tlahuelpuchi.

notes.title: RE:VIVE
notes.content:
So far, we've been creating the characters who will populate the world of [i]Mictlan [/i]using the sketches and drawings of our talented[b] concept art team[/b], along with [b]artificial intelligence[/b] to shape the faces of Mesoamerican people, obtaining amazing and realistic results.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38746200/f18b345bf08fe428ddd54fe75bdfb6bb78df99ca.jpg[/img]

[h3]But we want to [b]step this process up[/b].[/h3]

As our world becomes more and more connected through technological advances, it's becoming increasingly easy to get in touch with other people and cultures in different countries. The concept of diversity encompasses [b]acceptance[/b], [b]respect [/b]and [b]valorization[/b], understanding that each individual is unique. 

[h3][b]We want to capture[/b] the beauty and uniqueness of [b]indigenous people[/b], that's why we're very proud to launch our ambitious project called [b]RE:VIVE[/b].[/h3]

We're looking for [b]photographers[/b], [b]directors [/b]and any other artist who would like to collaborate with us in order to give us the opportunity to create even more realistic characters, [b]representing the Mexica civilizations[/b] as they properly deserve, through the use of photographs and 3d scanned photogrammetry rendering model.

[h3]It's not just about the game. [/h3]

The heart of the entire development process of [i]Mitclan [/i] lies on the [b]celebration of indigenous cultures[/b], by reviving thousand-years-old tales. 
Our goal with the project RE:VIVE is to [b]preserve the beauty[/b], the [b]uniqueness [/b]and the [b]culture [/b]of a civilization while creating an image data bank for future generations to see. 

Our [b][i]Mictlan [/i]agents[/b] will do so much more than capturing images and video: they will help our community to create a [b]powerful network [/b]of knowledge, beliefs, and people, under the [i][i]Mictlan [/i][/i]umbrella.

We will work with the [b]utmost respect[/b] toward our subjects, their communities, cultures and traditions.
Our mission is to allow people from all over the world to get to know Mexican and Mesoamerican history, [b]valuing our rich heritage[/b], ancient culture, practices but, most of all, [b]our people[/b].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38746200/be86cf7d282fe3d7e653cdc61f47431a83f27e9d.png[/img]

If anyone is interested in learning more about our RE:VIVE project, please contact us through one our official channels.

Stay tuned for more updates!

notes.title: Mexica priests with... dreadlocks?
notes.content:
Mexica priests with... dreadlocks? 

[b]Yes, please[/b].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38746200/c4c9809aee717cf89583cdd4e2cbddb63002f7c2.jpg[/img]

Our team of history [b]experts [/b]and [b]archaeologists [/b]has dug out these images taken from numerous Mesoamerican codices, depicting [b]Mexica priests[/b] ([i]Tlamacazqui[/i]) with [b]dreadlocks[/b].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38746200/aa135781e418fe41ee9844b1f63c463eb62e1a89.jpg[/img]

The Spanish friars who encountered them depicted the priests with [b]knee-length hair[/b], a trait commonly associated in popular culture with Rastafarian. 

Yet in many other cultures, such as Mesoamerican, aboriginal and Indian, people used to wear this hairstyle, considered as a [b]conduit with the divine[/b] and the ethereal. 

Even though dreadlocks take different meanings in each culture, the underlining essence between them relates to [b]resistance [/b]and [b]questioning of social stratification[/b].

[url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38746200/311e579520343c7c20643ddb5413c04677328e60.jpg][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38746200/67bd9b395f5f9f4f618b2ce4fc92e29a4b43fda6.jpg[/img][/url]   [url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38746200/2cf1812954e9a5e270500a1efb8b75ab48e0d124.jpg][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38746200/8bed81fec378e4e7378bbe226cdbde9dbcd2618b.jpg[/img][/url]   [url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38746200/b54b5fe35a22ebc911a7cd53bf765b0d2c37eae4.jpg][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38746200/f7664a1398e6ad5e9645cb2fceeb76d8bc653dce.jpg[/img][/url]

It is truly a [b]blessing [/b]for us to be able to work with a team of experts who are helping us to really bring the Mesoamerican spirit and culture to life and infuse our game with these elements.

Moreover, with these sources confirmed, rest assured that [b]you're gonna see some badass priests with dreads in [i]Mictlan[/i][/b]!

notes.title: The Franciscan Order
notes.content:
[b]The Franciscan Order [/b]is one of the most widely known religious orders in the Catholic Church, founded in [b]1209 [/b]by Saint Francis of Assisi. 

[b]Solidarity with the poor[/b] is an essential element of Franciscan Spirituality: the friars take the vow of poverty to work with the marginalized and help them improve their conditions.

The Franciscan Order was also the [b]first of the orders to arrive in New Spain[/b], taking control of the most important social and political centers in the Valley of Mexico, with the purpose of evangelizing the conquered territories. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38746200/8450133ce0bcac489298d55ae921426d2d7571b6.jpg[/img]

One of the most famous members of the Order was[b] Fray Bernandino de Sahagún[/b], who participated in the Catholic evangelization of colonial New Spain, spending his life in the central region of the Valley of Mexico, specifically in the convents of San Francisco Santiago Tlatelolco, Tepepulco, Xochimilco and Tlamanalco, among others.

Fray Bernandino de Sahagún is also known as the compiler of the [b][i]Historia general de las cosas de la Nueva España[/i][/b] ([i]The General History of the Things of New Spain[/i]): a codex consisting of 2,400 pages organized into twelve books, with approximately 2,500 illustrations drawn by native artists using both native and European techniques. Written both in [b]Spanish and Nahuatl[/b], the document is a testimony of the encounters with the new world and its people, and it stands out due to Sahagún's effort to gather information about a foreign culture by querying people [b]from within that culture[/b], interviewing native men who survived the Spanish conquest, to show their perspectives.

Due to the important cultural, social and religious [b]impact [/b]which the Franciscan Order had in the history of Mexico, we had to include the friars of this Order in the world of [i]Mictlan[/i], representing them with their traditional plain brown tunic with a hood, a cord fastened around the waist, and sandals.

notes.title: Ahuianime
notes.content:
One of the main features in [i]Mictlan: An Ancient Mythical Tale[/i], will be the possibility for the player to [b]interact[/b] with several creatures, deities and supernatural beings, but also with the [b]people [/b]living in the Mexica society during the 16th century. 

Today we want to talk about a very special group of women in Aztec culture: the [b]Ahuianime[/b].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38746200/5e78985b549d06e2091cea889605a780e41cf7ec.png[/img]

The Ahuianime were [b]embodiments of the goddess[/b] of beauty, fertility and carnal love, [b]Xochiquetzal[/b]. 
The sacred link between them and their patron goddess meant that they had a [b]significant role in religious festivals[/b] and rituals, especially those involving human sacrifice.

As a matter of fact, the Ahuianime were the [b]attendants of deity impersonators destined for sacrifice[/b]. They were chosen to comfort, amuse and encourage those men, and were afterward rewarded by receiving all the precious belongings of the impersonators after their death. The Ahuianime were present in many festivities such as [i]Izcalli[/i], with the duty to care for the impersonator’s every need through [b]their presence[/b] but also [b]their arts[/b] such as music, dance and cooking.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38746200/46bdeb7e552e7109279daadf10836600048cd2c3.png[/img]

Ahuianime would wear their [b]long hair down[/b] and adorn their bodies with pieces of jewelry, perfuming themselves with [b]fragrant herbs and flowers[/b]. They pleased the hearts of the gods with complex [b]dances[/b], fascinating all the successful warriors and noblemen watching them wearing their [b]colorful dresses[/b] with intricate embroidery, flowers, feathers and other ornaments. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38746200/7f0f72365b8f657963a2b2f2bebb654198d534f9.png[/img]

In the Aztecs'[b]warfare-centered [/b]culture and society, the Ahuianime would also [b]travel with the armies[/b] as camp servants, to encourage and motivate soldiers to go into battle and, occasionally, in desperate times, may even have served as [b]warriors [/b]in their own right.

Even if their lifestyle in many ways contradicted the [i]Tlacoqualli in monequi[/i] (“[b]The moderation is proper/The middle good is necessary[/b]") - which established Nahua's desired behavior - there is still a lot of mystery surrounding the figure of the Ahuianime and how their behavior was perceived. But whether they were openly accepted or frowned upon, the [b]sacredness and the importance[/b] of this group of Aztec women, who were trained and educated to entertain others and spread joy in all forms,[b] is undeniable[/b].

notes.title: Xoloitzcuintli
notes.content:
Today we're introducing you to a very[b] special companion[/b]. 

The faithful one who has been accompanying mankind for at least[b] 3,000 years[/b]. 
The one that will be by your side in your adventures in [i][b]Mictlan[/b][/i].

[h3]The very special creature we're talking about is the [b]Xoloitzcuintli[/b]. [/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38746200/ab7c279e37186b6eac394b7fb0db82c99b87eece.jpg[/img]

The Xoloitzcuintli, or[b] Mexican Hairless dog[/b], is one of the oldest and rarest dog breeds in the world. 
It received its name from the Aztec god [b]Xolotl [/b]who, according to the myth, created the dog to guard the living and, most importantly, to [b]guide the souls of the dead[/b] through the dangers of [i]Mictlán[/i], the Underworld. 

Legend has it that, when creating The Fifth Sun, [b]Xolotl[/b] and [b]Quetzalcoatl [/b]descended to the Underworld to [b]collect bones of ancient humans[/b], which they used to restore mankind. The Xoloitzcuintli was created from those same bones and presented as a [b]gift from the gods to humans[/b].

Xoloitzcuintli was not only a faithful companion in life, but it accompanied men in the dangerous journey through the Underworld, the place where the souls of the dead went in their [b]afterlife[/b].
The deceased souls and their dog companion would wander side by side, traveling through the [b]nine levels [/b]of the Underworld for four years, before finally reaching their [b]ultimate destination[/b]: Mictlan.

They had to overcome a series of obstacles and challenges in order to [b]ultimately free their soul[/b].

[h3]Take a look at our WIP of the Xoloitzcuintli![/h3]

notes.title: Ahuizotl
notes.content:
Today we're showing you the first WIP images of an ancient, legendary creature: 

[h3][b]Ahuizotl[/b], the [b]Thorny One of the Water[/b][/h3]

The Ahuizotl is often represented as a lethal creature with spiky fur: it resembles a [b]dog [/b]with a slick body and pointed ears, but in place of canine paws, the Ahuizotl has hands and feet like a [b]monkey[/b]'s.

This creature is believed to have [b]haunted many fishermen's sleep[/b]. 

It would use its long, prehensile tail to grab its unsuspecting victims to pull them under the water. It would hold them there, until they [b]drowned[/b]. The Ahuizotl would then [b]feast on its prey's eyes, nails and teeth[/b], leaving the rest of the body floating in the water.

notes.title: Creating realistic, compelling characters
notes.content:
We believe that creating [b]believable characters[/b] is the best way to evoke genuine emotion and reaction from players. Visual attributes can be purposely used in order to communicate aspects of a character's personality, producing a more [b]immersive and enjoyable gameplay[/b]. 

That's why the[b] anatomy and appearance[/b] of [i]Mictlan[/i]'s characters is the result of thorough research and planning, achieved by studying [b]pre-Hispanic codices[/b] and colonial writings.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38746200/e76141bc3260ab180463d8f8a16b977b583eb316.jpg[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38746200/631faa4686821d31bbcc997e56663818ec611521.jpg[/img]

This research has led us to discover that body modification and attires used by early civilizations carried with them not only social symbols and status, but they spoke of people's literacy, wealth, and also their [b]religion[/b]. 

The body was a vessel for the most precious gift the Gods game men: [b]life[/b].

The study of anthropomorphic imagery in Mesoamerican cultures offers meaningful information and a better understanding of personhood, conceptions of the body, and[b] relationships between humans, nature, and the divine[/b].

[url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1411900?emclan=103582791468267608&emgid=3026951542954716803]The artificial alteration of physical appearance[/url] was of the utmost social importance in the Mesoamerican world, it transcended pure aesthetics and was imbued with social significance, religious beliefs and also had a [b]divine function[/b]: it represented a bridge, a medium between the natural and divine worlds.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38746200/e99542d82526e23510fc4458353dbc5c67d53709.jpg[/img][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38746200/cd213f305d7b40ea9519c71f464ce3b84f2d4707.jpg[/img]

Taking into account these kinds of research, the work of our talented [b]concept artists [/b]becomes a process of creativity in which designers come up with scenarios, attires and color schemes appropriate to the historical period in which our story takes place. 

They proceed by modeling a[b] three-dimensional mesh[/b] for each object, natural and architectural elements. They define the anatomy and bone structure of animals and people, shaping their [b]realistic movements[/b]. Final touches are added by adjusting the colors, textures and lighting for each scene. 

Of course, everything is also adjusted to meet aesthetic criteria, game-related necessities and the amount of realism that we wish to convey.

[url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38746200/1c2196772080e9b88d4c00e45a56171c4f67c6e7.jpg][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38746200/11ea0ac30d147f7a22ac13afcafd0d21d4eb3c80.jpg[/img][/url] [url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38746200/16bf71f19398f8d1c33ca32cdbba918de27f7ce1.jpg][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38746200/d8656ab21aa73946311030be6d2f2910cac23fb4.jpg[/img][/url] [url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38746200/74df0c3668e02e6f5b47e9db281752ec26a2e32d.jpg][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38746200/4e69fd490350b8554503f3146d71246a9b16b26d.jpg[/img][/url] [url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38746200/1a92f49138f0531ecf56b2ed9c25ee47b0b74164.jpg][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38746200/7917880e02cd562346b4c30043f97600d87cdaab.jpg[/img][/url] [url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38746200/fbf86135f12f87fc2ef3148c9595e49364c0e9ec.jpg][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38746200/4e518f5823feb35d149d6c727d12804f8b0f9b92.jpg[/img][/url]

[url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38746200/45d11799d6f9be5eff388817d179e6565215e359.jpg][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38746200/d06f3bd098b483bf24e454e436f2c2e7724d78a3.jpg[/img][/url] [url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38746200/e89b39ede5cbd6b4a90f44b16fbfc476fccd923d.jpg][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38746200/783f54e1b2b14a4f957ac5e82e187bc9913b7a06.jpg[/img][/url] [url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38746200/86fac352dffe75992d6e08acbe7ef0fbbbde4296.jpg][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38746200/f6730629d32ad61eeeabedc32cb2943c022fe2dd.jpg[/img][/url] [url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38746200/184ae988b253ce148c8c4fa9bf892947b3e600c7.jpg][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38746200/18f4deb3ca7dc18efad84b85d95c834a7fa05d5e.jpg[/img][/url] [url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38746200/a702f14068ac7f3da75f38101a8651b30f6b8d08.jpg][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38746200/edaa07a3a24e0653766c62abdbdd967e55dacf2d.jpg[/img][/url] 

The creative process, resulting from dynamic and collaborative teamwork, is aimed at developing [b]interesting and compelling characters [/b]in which players can identify. When you immerse into a video game, you want to become one of the characters who exist within that universe, a character you get to know and share an epic journey and experience with. 

[h3]The immersion into another world, is all about characters.[/h3]

In the case of [i]Mictlan[/i], players will be able to travel back in time, living, breathing a[b] mythical tale[/b], immersing themselves in the [b]history and identity of ancient Mexico[/b].

notes.title: An immersive journey through the pioneering sounds of Etnica
notes.content:
If you close your eyes and listen to the [b]unearthly, cosmic sounds[/b] of this soundtrack, they will take you to a distant, perilous land on an epic and[b] immersive journey[/b].

We are overwhelmingly proud and excited to announce our collaboration with two of the most talented music producers, [b]pioneers of Goa trance psychedelic music[/b], pillars of the music scene since the 80s:

[h3][b]Etnica[/b][/h3]

Etnica group is composed of Ibiza-based (Soundfarm Studios) producers [b]Max Lanfranconi[/b] and [b]Maurizio Begotti [/b]from Milan, Italy. 

Max and Maurizio are currently working on the production of [b][i]Mictlan[/i]'s soundtrack[/b], lending their knowledge and experience to [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1411900?emclan=103582791468267608&emgid=3025824821127869256]our music team[/url].

Their thorough research on [b]ancient sounds[/b] from Mexico and Latin America has resulted in a perfect mix of sounds for the Mesoamerican world in which our story takes place.

[i]Mictlan[/i]'s soundtrack will be a huge part of the game and its vibe, setting a mythical tone for you, the players, who will live a [b]unique sensory experience[/b], taking you to cross the line between life and death, truly entering the dark world of [i]Mictlan[/i].

notes.title: NPC: Fisherman infected with smallpox
notes.content:
Here is a work in progress of a 3D model character, based on a NPC [b]fisherman who has been infected with smallpox[/b], a very infectious disease reaching the Americas in the 1500s. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38746200/f5e7f972c4fe5cb06550ebfdc9262f6b3df1ecf3.jpg[/img]

Since indigenous people had no natural immunity against smallpox, historians have estimated that this disease and other European diseases [b]reduced the indigenous population[/b] of North and South America by up to[b] 90 percent[/b]. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38746200/7cd47b55f4bfdb59aab70995947a2006cacd0b41.jpg[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38746200/14dbe3801c2229d2edb83cabc8e8598f21214ede.jpg[/img]

We are very proud of our character development (have you already checked[url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1411900/view/3025824821129123543] our post about Tezcatlipoca[/url], for example?) and our team is always working hard to create the most [b]accurate and amazing characters[/b] for [i]Mictlan[/i].

notes.title: NPC: Noble Toltec Warrior
notes.content:
Today we're happy to present to you our NPC [b]Noble Toltec Warrior[/b]!

The model was designed on the basis of the iconography present in the archaeological site [b]Tula, Hidalgo[/b]. The character was created by our good friend, Salvadorean Artist, [b]Daniel Posada[/b], who managed to combine the archaeological evidence with fantasy elements to give life to our Noble Toltec Warrior. 

[url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38746200/c103c9791df3f493eecc9e6272eb84853b8c815e.jpg][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38746200/30054f4c878696a2c32151c3cf290fb0eb677358.jpg[/img][/url]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38746200/df57e03f35b49a3d3ff096b4a11166286f6186ee.png[/img]

It is known that prehispanic civilizations used to send [b]ambassadors [/b]to negotiate treaties, encourage trade, deal with war and peace issues, therefore we imagined our Toltec Warrior as some sort of emissary for the Empire: an [b]old war veteran[/b] who fought many battles and who's now become a noble warrior.

notes.title: Scarification, tattooing, body paint
notes.content:
As Laura Caso Barrera has pointed out in the paper titled "Body Treatment and Social Control among. the Maya Itza, XVII-XVIII Centuries":

[quote][i]In many societies, the human body is considered as a cosmological model and therefore of society. In the case of the Maya Itza we know that the human body is a reference to their territorial, social and religious organization.[/i][/quote]
Pre-columbian civilizations of Central and South America paid careful attention to their [b]appearance[/b] and used many different ornaments or permanent decorations to beautify the body and to indicate the social rank of an individual. 

As a matter of fact, the[b] artificial alteration of physical appearance[/b] was of the utmost social importance in the Mesoamerican world. Early societies developed different forms of body modifications and treatments to represent their very own characteristics: [b]scarification[/b], [b]tattooing[/b], [b]pierced [/b]noses, ears, and lips, and [b]body paint[/b].

Body paint were donned for special occasions to [b]mark the status[/b] of the wearer: they were used in battles, for example, and the application of a specific face paint was an indication of martial success.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38746200/140b2cc1af3ba465204cb1b2e5b8fcf36ce0f48a.jpg[/img]

Even though we are developing a video game, not a documentary, it is very important for us and duty as Mexicans to do our best to incorporate in [i]Mictlan[/i] [b]details of cultural and historical relevance[/b], along with a cool and [b]interesting story[/b], intertwined with [b]fantasy [/b]elements.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38746200/cd0a6f262456f8cc4b55695a8e992147f17984bc.jpg[/img]

We want to convey a sense of [b]authenticity [/b]which will allow both Mexican and non-Mexican gamers to appreciate the ancient Mesoamerican cultures. That's why each model, piece of clothing and accessory we design is the result of a [b]thorough research[/b].

Today we are sharing with you the work of our teammate [b]Jorge “Coco” Velázquez[/b], who did an outstanding job of codex research, while artistically recreating these examples of [b]face paint[/b] in our ancient pre-Hispanic culture.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38746200/c4a0de8af06f9d1f1d74e14aa4602c0a00c6a1dc.jpg[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38746200/72251a7ea4286231787bd0980124d9ad131888f5.jpg[/img]

[h3]Which of these you would like to see more of? Let us know in the comments![/h3]

The lovely "grannie" you see in the picture will be a very effective [b]healer [/b]in the world of [i]Mictlan[/i].

This character is inspired by the [b]Cihuatlamacazque[/b], the priestesses in ancient Mexico who devoted their lives to guard and serve the [b]temples [/b]and sanctuaries. Among their duties, they wove blankets in gaudy colors for the use of the temple. At midnight each night, they threw incense on the braziers before the idols.

If you happen to encounter one of these priestesses in your travels, passing through villages and forests, they will[b] heal your wounds[/b], [b]regenerate your stamina[/b] and even help you gain [b]special and magical powers[/b] that you'll certainly find useful in your adventures.

notes.title: Tezcatlipoca: God of the Night Sky
notes.content:
Today we are proud to present to you one of the main deities of the Aztec pantheon, who will also have a key role as a character in [i]Mictlan[/i]: [b]Tezcatlipoca[/b].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38746200/7c98662c614613924a33bdcf4bf84f56bb62793b.jpg[/img]

Tezcatlipoca was among the merciless ancient Gods who [b]demanded blood[/b]. As a matter of fact, the practice of [b]human sacrifice[/b] was introduced into central Mexico under his influence.

God of the constellation of the Great Bear and the night sky, his name means "[b]Smoking Mirror[/b]" in Nahuatl. It refers to mirrors made of [b]obsidian[/b], a shiny black stone that Aztec priests used in [i]divination[/i]. 
Tezcatlipoca himself, a mischievous and mysterious figure, [b]knew all the deeds and thoughts of humankind[/b]: he could see everything happening on Earth and intervene directly in human affairs, bringing both happiness or [b]sorrow[/b]. Always present, always watching, he took delight in causing [b]conflict [/b]and confusion.  
As you can see from the model, we recreated an obsidian belt representing his powers of [b]omnipotence[/b]. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38746200/78c5f6831ede8b3532fe83e23753b04ed69fede3.jpg[/img]

Although it was believed that Tezcatlipoca could take on a bewildering array of manifestations, he has often been associated with the [b]color black[/b] and the [b]jaguar[/b]. As a matter of fact, Tezcatlipoca’s [i]nagual[/i], his sacred animal spirit, was a jaguar. That is why we included a piece of clothing in spotted jaguar skin, which has also been compared to the starry sky.

You may also notice that Tezcatlipoca has [b]one foot missing[/b]. According to the myth, he lost his foot when he used it as bait for the reptilian monster [i]Cipactli[/i], which he later dismembered to create the World. 

(Did you know that the colossal [b]sea monster Cipactli[/b] will actually be in our game? You can take a look at our concept art and read more about her and the myth of the Creation [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1411900?emclan=103582791468267608&emgid=3030327786399574702]in this post[/url]!)

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38746200/d96a2883b384ceb83c3e7687de7fdfdf0ba1cf7c.jpg[/img]

In our model, Tezcatlipoca's missing foot is replaced by a [b]coyote foot[/b], because it is said that another of the God's manifestation in animal form was a coyote. In a benevolent act, he would place itself in the path of travelers, blocking their way. That's how travelers understood that danger of some sort lay ahead, and that the [b]God was warning them[/b]. 

Tezcatlipoca's head is also adorned with resplendent [b]quetzal[/b] feathers: a magnificent, emerald plumed bird venerated by Aztecs and Mayans.

Lastly, you may notice a very particular [b]skull[/b] nestled in Tezcatlipoca's unsettling mask. That is the most common representation of Tezcatlipoca, who is often portrayed wearing a turquoise mask with a black eye band. In the image below, you can see one of the most famous art objects of the God, which is a decorated skull displayed in the [i]British Museum [/i]in London.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38746200/b595b20657e1764baf25e84796d88d1a1f01a3cd.jpg[/img]

The reference for our 3D model of Tezcatlipoca was the[b] concept art [/b]of our incredible Art Director and and lead concept artist [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1411900?emclan=103582791468267608&emgid=3030327786392021270]Yashaswi Karthik[/url]. 
We put so much effort and attention to details in order to offer you a [b]AAA quality character[/b], because we believe [i]Mictlan [/i]deserves it! We hope you appreciate the hard work and energy we are pouring into this project. We are just a [i]small indie studio[/i], not a multimillion-dollar one, but our team is still doing everything possible to match the [b]quality standards[/b] of the international gaming industry.

notes.content:

notes.title: Can you believe who's joining our game?
notes.content:
[h3]Dear all, today we are very excited to share with you [b]a big news[/b]![/h3]

We can finally unveil our partnership with[b] Horacio García Rojas[/b], as he's going to be [b]a main character[/b] in our game! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38746200/c7a35e973be43ed5cffe0e3e89f607fa78be09ab.jpg[/img]

Horacio is a talented, handsome actor known for his roles in series like [i][b]Diablero[/b] [/i]and [i][b]Narcos: México[/b][/i], as well as for his outstanding performance as the Tlamemeh Painalli, in the 2016 Alan Jonsson Gavica film [i][b]La Carga[/b][/i].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38746200/f89c7a8e193f119914266bef97ef9e2025d5d324.jpg[/img]

His role as one of the first leading actor with dark skin in a Neflix original series has been crucial to [b]break stereotypes[/b] commonly relegating actors with darker skin to roles as villains. Horacio's work makes viewers appreciate both the[b] cultural richness[/b] that exists in Mexico City and in the country.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38746200/14c263e9516b2fed73da31195d8637f865581491.jpg[/img]

[b]Proudly Mexican[/b], [b]proudly Mestizo[/b], Horacio García Rojas uphold the good name of México and of its culture and traditions, taking them to the big screen as an actor. 

Now he will also [b]lend his talents to our videogame[/b] and that's why we feel extremely honored, proud and grateful counting on our collaboration in [i]Mictlan[/i].

It's also worth mentioning that Horacio is a big fan of comic books and geek culture, he's also part of the gaming community!

[h3]We look forward to great things to come from our partnership![/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38746200/7137353b2de9e449f37866cc41503b329903955b.jpg[/img]

notes.title: Cipactli
notes.content:
The world and underworld of [i]Mictlan [/i]will be populated by the most amazing creatures waiting to make your acquaintance. While some of them are just downright cute (have you seen our [b][url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1411900/Mictlan_An_Ancient_Mythical_Tale/]Axolotl[/url][/b]?), others may be a little, well, [b]a whole lot scarier[/b]!

Today we are excited to present to you [b]Cipactli[/b]: a voracious, colossal, primeval sea monster, part fish, part crocodile, with gaping mouths at all her joints. 

The embodiment of [b]chaos [/b]existing before the creation.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38746200/9e117a4d6840387949241d2e43e9eac70f899ce5.jpg[/img]

This monstrous being was conceived as female, and it was so insatiable that, one day, the gods [i]Quetzalcoatl [/i]and [i]Tezcatlipoca [/i]set out to [b]destroy her[/b], descending from the heavens to ban this horrible creature from roaming the world. The two of them, assuming the form of serpents, coiling themselves about Cipactli as she lay on the surface, ripped her body apart. 

The upper part of her body ascended to become the [b]sky[/b], while its other half fell to become the [b]earth[/b]. From the hair of the monster, the gods created trees, from her eyes springs and caves, from her mouth rivers and lakes, from her nose valleys, from her shoulders volcanos and mountains.

Nevertheless, it is said that otherworldly sounds of Cipactli's crying could still be heard, [b]demanding human blood[/b], wishing to devour human hearts as[b] repayment for her sacrifice[/b].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38746200/7c6dc078d76ec7781f6f64c46062bb547114bd7f.jpg[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38746200/be86cf7d282fe3d7e653cdc61f47431a83f27e9d.png[/img]

We would like to remind you that we are getting closer to our [b]Kickstarter [/b]goal, but we still need more subscribers! For those who have not registered, it is very important that you do so, [url=https://www.kickstarter.com/projects/mictlanthegame/micltan-the-video-game?fbclid=IwAR1t3wZek4efNtMOmjXDk7HyclzrLfug5IL8e4M_zB2BIydeFMzGwmi5Pqc]it only takes a few minutes[/url]. It is a necessary step to be able to launch our campaign and raise the necessary funds to develop Mictlan!

[b]Thank you very much for all your support![/b]

notes.title: Meet the Axolotl
notes.content:
The world of Mictlan will be populated by the most amazing, dangerous, ancient creatures... and also the [b]cutest ones[/b]!

Meet the [b]Axolotl[/b], the funny, adorable little guy who will accompany you both across the wide, wondrous world and the perilous underworld of Mictlan. You'll have the chance to mount the Axolotl as you dive through the depths of the ocean.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38746200/10602a2640c445efa3f215757f1f8fb7a662874b.jpg[/img]

We have finalized the [b]animations [/b]for our lovely walking fish thanks to the help of a very special member of our team: [b]Axel[/b], the pet Axolotl we keep in our studio! He's almost two years old and we carefully studied its movements to recreate a more fluid and realistic animation of the Axolotl in our game! Take a look [url=https://www.facebook.com/watch/?v=181958486736813]here[/url], and [url=https://www.facebook.com/108104087681598/videos/2652458918398583]here[/url].

notes.content:
[h1]Mictlan’s semi-open world[/h1]

We are very excited to share with you the [b]layout of the game map[/b] we’ve been working on so far! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38746200/0fca391ab87820b8ac8821a9c0910487409f88bb.png[/img]

Here are some WIP images from Mictlan’s semi-open world, currently measuring [b]30 square KM[/b]! 
We plan to expand the game map to the North of the country and various areas of Central America, such as [i]Tikal [/i]in Guatemala and [i]El Mirador,[/i] which is home to the largest pyramid in the world. 
You’ll be free to roam from southern Mexico and Guatemala to the northern deserts of Mexico. 

Of course there will be [b]plenty to explore[/b] in these vast lands and, in future expansion packs, we plan to represent [b]different indigenous groups[/b] from the North of Mexico, such as[i] Seri[/i] and [i]Yaqui [/i]people.
